blocks.x: Role-scoped agents that execute process steps under explicit policy bounds: permissions derived from the role, checkpoints placed by risk, replay for every action, and an exception queue designed for humans — not a chat window bolted to an RPA bot.
An agent is a junior employee with perfect attendance — staff it like one

An agent in a business process is a junior employee with perfect memory and no judgment — until you give it judgment-shaped tools, at which point it also needs supervision. We design agents as roles: explicit responsibilities, explicit tool grants, explicit escalation paths, and a supervisor loop that inspects work before it commits.

The build discipline is boring by design: each agent's permissions are the minimum that lets it do its role, its actions are idempotent, its retries are bounded, and every decision it makes can be replayed from the trace. Agents that fail these tests do not graduate from staging.
Below: the failure modes that make agent programs fragile, the reference architecture that makes them defensible, and the console that shows exactly what the digital staff did today.
Four failure modes that erode agent programs
Each of these starts small and compounds quietly; the countermeasures are structural, because by the time the failure is visible in the KPIs the checkpoints have already eroded.

blocks.x: Reference architecture — policy-bounded execution with risk-placed checkpoints

Two design decisions carry the architecture: agent scopes are derived from role definitions rather than granted ad hoc, and checkpoint placement follows a risk matrix signed by the process owner — so autonomy is earned by evidence, step by step.

widgets.title: Anatomy of one governed run — click each stage

stages.name: Goal intake
stages.detail: The run starts as a typed request object — goal, constraints, deadline, budget class — not a free-text prompt. Typed intake is what makes replay and cost accounting possible.

stages.name: Plan
stages.detail: Planner emits a step graph with tool candidates per node; the policy layer strikes any tool the credentials of this run class cannot touch, before execution begins.

stages.name: Execute
stages.detail: Every write carries an idempotency key; every read is cached by content hash. Retries are budgeted — the third retry of the same call escalates instead.

stages.name: Verify
stages.detail: Critic asserts output shape and business checks (totals reconcile, dates in range); the policy gate re-checks scope before any side effect lands.

stages.name: Ledger
stages.detail: Inputs, plan revisions, tool I/O, model versions and cost are sealed into the run record — the artifact an auditor or incident review reads first.

widgets.note: The five stages are the same for a $0.10 data-entry run and a $4 exception run — only the budgets differ.

blocks.x: Agent stack defaults — and documented deviations
Defaults bias toward typed tool access and bounded autonomy; deviations are permitted where the process argues for them, with the risk delta written next to each trigger condition.

blocks.caption: Agentic Process Automation: default stack and the conditions under which we deviate
rows: Agent runtime
Typed planning loop with bounded steps (LangGraph-class)
Simple rule-bots for tasks with no ambiguity — agents are not free
Tool access
Scoped, expiring grants via gateway; deny by default
Shared service accounts — they destroy the audit trail
Verification
In-flow reconciliation against source systems
Trusting the model's self-report — it is the failure mode
Identity
One principal per agent; short-lived credentials
Agent-as-user accounts — policy cannot bind what it cannot see
Escalation
Structured handoff with full trace to the human desk
Raw error dumps — supervisors need the reasoning trail

blocks.caption: Release gates for Agentic Process Automation — the evidence each demands
rows: Grant gate
Is every tool call within a scoped, expiring grant?
Grant ledger; recertification record; deny-by-default test
Verifier gate
Does verification cover every committing action?
Verifier map per action class; reconciliation evidence
Chaos gate
Does it survive token revocation and tool outage?
Drill reports: degradation path, queue resume time
Cost gate
Is the ceiling binding?
Per-run cost telemetry; breaker test at ceiling
Replay gate
Can any committed action be reconstructed?
Sampled replay with inputs, plan, tool calls and outcomes
